{{short description|Concept in physics}}
[[File:Backtang2.png|thumb|An image of the 2d [[Bak-Tang-Wiesenfeld sandpile]], the original model of self-organized criticality.]]
{{Complex systems}}

'''Self-organized criticality''' ('''SOC''') is a property of [[dynamical system]]s that have a [[critical phenomena|critical point]] as an [[attractor]].  Their macroscopic behavior thus displays the spatial or temporal [[scale invariance|scale-invariance]] characteristic of the [[critical point (physics)|critical point]] of a [[phase transition]], but without the need to tune control parameters to a precise value, because the system, effectively, tunes itself as it evolves towards criticality.

The concept was put forward by [[Per Bak]], [[Chao Tang]] and [[Kurt Wiesenfeld]] ("BTW") in a paper<ref name=Bak1987>
{{cite journal | vauthors = Bak P, Tang C, Wiesenfeld K | title = Self-organized criticality: An explanation of the 1/f noise | journal = Physical Review Letters | volume = 59 | issue = 4 | pages = 381–384 | date = July 1987 | pmid = 10035754 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.59.381 | bibcode = 1987PhRvL..59..381B }},</ref> following an earlier paper<ref name=Katz1986> {{cite journal | vauthors = Katz, J I | title =  A Model of Propagating Brittle Failure in Heterogeneous Media | journal = Journal of Geophysical Research | volume = 91 | pages = 10412-10420 | date = September 1986 | doi = 10.1029/JB091iB10p10412 | bibcode = 1986JGR....9110412K}}</ref> by Jonathan I. Katz published in 1987 in ''[[Physical Review Letters]]'', and is considered to be one of the mechanisms by which [[complexity]]<ref name=Bak1995>
{{cite journal | vauthors = Bak P, Paczuski M | title = Complexity, contingency, and criticality | journal = Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America | volume = 92 | issue = 15 | pages = 6689–6696 | date = July 1995 | pmid = 11607561 | pmc = 41396 | doi = 10.1073/pnas.92.15.6689 | doi-access = free | bibcode = 1995PNAS...92.6689B }}</ref> arises in nature. Its concepts have been applied across fields as diverse as [[geophysics]],<ref name=SmalleyTurcotteSolla85>{{cite journal | vauthors = Smalley Jr RF, Turcotte DL, Solla SA |author3-link=Sara Solla | year = 1985| title = A renormalization group approach to the stick-slip behavior of faults
| journal = Journal of Geophysical Research | bibcode = 1985JGR....90.1894S | doi = 10.1029/JB090iB02p01894 | volume = 90 | issue = B2 | pages = 1894–1900 |s2cid=28835238}}</ref><ref name=SmythNashMoum2019>{{cite journal | vauthors = Smyth WD, Nash JD, Moum JN | title = Self-organized criticality in geophysical turbulence | journal = Scientific Reports | volume = 9 | issue = 1 | page = 3747 | date = March 2019 | pmid = 30842462 | pmc = 6403305 | doi = 10.1038/s41598-019-39869-w  | doi-access = free| name-list-style = amp | bibcode = 2019NatSR...9.3747S }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Hatamian |first=S. T. |date=February 1996 |title=Modeling fragmentation in two dimensions |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/BF00876672 |journal=Pure and Applied Geophysics PAGEOPH |language=en |volume=146 |issue=1 |pages=115–129 |doi=10.1007/BF00876672 |bibcode=1996PApGe.146..115H |issn=0033-4553|url-access=subscription }}</ref> [[physical cosmology]], [[evolutionary biology]] and [[ecology]], [[bio-inspired computing]] and [[optimization (mathematics)]], [[economics]], [[quantum gravity]], [[sociology]], [[solar physics]], [[plasma physics]], [[neurobiology]]<ref>{{Cite journal| vauthors = Dmitriev A, Dmitriev V |date=2021-01-20|title=Identification of Self-Organized Critical State on Twitter Based on the Retweets' Time Series Analysis|journal=Complexity|language=en|volume=2021|article-number=e6612785|doi=10.1155/2021/6612785|issn=1076-2787|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal| vauthors = Shapoval A, Le Mouel JL, Shnirman MG, Courtillot V|date=2018-11-01|title=Observational evidence in favor of scale-free evolution of sunspot groups|journal=Astronomy and Astrophysics|language=en|volume=618|pages=A183|doi=10.1051/0004-6361/201832799|doi-access=free|bibcode=2018A&A...618A.183S |issn=0004-6361}}</ref><ref name=LinkenkaerHansen2001>{{cite journal | vauthors = Linkenkaer-Hansen K, Nikouline VV, Palva JM, Ilmoniemi RJ | title = Long-range temporal correlations and scaling behavior in human brain oscillations | journal = The Journal of Neuroscience | volume = 21 | issue = 4 | pages = 1370–1377 | date = February 2001 | pmid = 11160408 | pmc = 6762238 | doi = 10.1523/JNEUROSCI.21-04-01370.2001 | name-list-style = amp }}</ref><ref name=Beggs2003>{{cite journal | vauthors = Beggs JM, Plenz D | title = Neuronal avalanches in neocortical circuits | journal = The Journal of Neuroscience | volume = 23 | issue = 35 | pages = 11167–11177 | date = December 2003 | pmid = 14657176 | pmc = 6741045 | doi = 10.1523/JNEUROSCI.23-35-11167.2003 | name-list-style = amp }}</ref><ref name=Chialvo2004>{{cite journal | vauthors = Chialvo DR | year = 2004 | title = Critical brain networks | journal = Physica A | volume = 340 | issue = 4 | pages = 756&ndash;765 | doi = 10.1016/j.physa.2004.05.064|arxiv = cond-mat/0402538 |bibcode = 2004PhyA..340..756R | s2cid = 15922916 | author-link = Dante R. Chialvo }}</ref> and others.

SOC is typically observed in slowly driven [[non-equilibrium thermodynamics|non-equilibrium]] systems with many [[degrees of freedom (physics and chemistry)|degrees of freedom]] and strongly [[nonlinearity|nonlinear]] dynamics.  Many individual examples have been identified since BTW's original paper, but to date there is no known set of general characteristics that ''guarantee'' a system will display SOC.

== Overview ==

Self-organized criticality is one of a number of important discoveries made in [[statistical physics]] and related fields over the latter half of the 20th century, discoveries which relate particularly to the study of [[complexity]] in nature.  For example, the study of [[cellular automata]], from the early discoveries of [[Stanislaw Ulam]] and [[John von Neumann]] through to [[John Horton Conway|John Conway]]'s [[Conway's Game of Life|Game of Life]] and the extensive work of [[Stephen Wolfram]], made it clear that complexity could be generated as an [[emergence|emergent]] feature of extended systems with simple local interactions.  Over a similar period of time, [[Benoît Mandelbrot]]'s large body of work on [[fractals]] showed that much complexity in nature could be described by certain ubiquitous mathematical laws, while the extensive study of [[phase transition]]s carried out in the 1960s and 1970s showed how [[scale invariance|scale invariant]] phenomena such as [[fractals]] and [[power law]]s emerged at the [[critical point (physics)|critical point]] between phases.

The term ''self-organized criticality'' was first introduced in [[Per Bak|Bak]], [[Chao Tang|Tang]] and [[Kurt Wiesenfeld|Wiesenfeld]]'s 1987 paper, which clearly linked together those factors: a simple [[cellular automaton]] was shown to produce several characteristic features observed in natural complexity ([[fractal]] geometry, [[pink noise|pink (1/f) noise]] and [[power law]]s) in a way that could be linked to [[critical point (physics)|critical-point phenomena]]. Crucially, however, the paper emphasized that the complexity observed emerged in a robust manner that did not depend on finely tuned details of the system: variable parameters in the model could be changed widely without affecting the emergence of critical behavior: hence, ''[[self-organized]]'' criticality. Thus, the key result of BTW's paper was its discovery of a mechanism by which the emergence of complexity from simple local interactions could be ''spontaneous''&mdash;and therefore plausible as a source of natural complexity&mdash;rather than something that was only possible in artificial situations in which control parameters are tuned to precise critical values. An alternative view is that SOC appears when the criticality is linked to a value of zero of the control parameters.<ref name=Gabrielli2000>
{{cite journal | vauthors = Gabrielli A, Caldarelli G, Pietronero L | title = Invasion percolation with temperature and the nature of self-organized criticality in real systems | journal = Physical Review E | volume = 62 | issue = 6 Pt A | pages = 7638–7641 | date = December 2000 | pmid = 11138032 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevE.62.7638 | arxiv = cond-mat/9910425 | bibcode = 2000PhRvE..62.7638G | s2cid = 20510811 }}</ref>

Despite the considerable interest and research output generated from the SOC hypothesis, there remains no general agreement with regards to its mechanisms in abstract mathematical form.  Bak, Tang and Wiesenfeld based their hypothesis on the behavior of their sandpile model.<ref name=Bak1987/>

== Mathematical models ==
In chronological order of development:

* [[Invasion percolation]]
* Stick-slip model of fault failure<ref name="TurcotteSmalleySolla85" /><ref name="SmalleyTurcotteSolla85" />
*[[Abelian sandpile model|Bak–Tang–Wiesenfeld sandpile]]
* [[Forest-fire model]]
* Manna model<ref>S.S. Manna, J. Phys. A, Math. Gen. 24(7), L363 (1991)</ref>
* [[Olami–Feder–Christensen model]]
* [[Bak–Sneppen model]]
* [[Neural network]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Freddi |first=Ruggero |last2=Cicala |first2=Francesco |last3=Marzetti |first3=Laura |last4=Basti |first4=Alessio |date=2025-10-06 |title=A mean-field approach to criticality in spiking neural networks for reservoir computing |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-18004-y |journal=Scientific Reports |language=en |volume=15 |issue=1 |page=34709 |doi=10.1038/s41598-025-18004-y  |doi-access=free|issn=2045-2322|pmc=12501264 }}</ref>
* The rice pile<ref>V. Frette, K. Christensen, A. Malthe-Sørenssen, J. Feder, T. Jøssang, P. Meakin, Nature 379, 49 (1996)</ref> or Oslo model<ref>K. Christensen, Á. Corral, V. Frette, J. Feder, T. Jøssang, Phys. Rev. Lett. 77(1), 107 (1996)</ref>

Early theoretical work included the development of a variety of alternative SOC-generating dynamics distinct from the BTW model, attempts to prove model properties analytically (including calculating the [[critical exponent]]s<ref name=Tang1988a>
{{cite journal | vauthors = Tang C, Bak P | title = Critical exponents and scaling relations for self-organized critical phenomena | journal = Physical Review Letters | volume = 60 | issue = 23 | pages = 2347–2350 | date = June 1988 | pmid = 10038328 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.60.2347 | bibcode = 1988PhRvL..60.2347T }}
</ref><ref name=Tang1988b>{{cite journal | vauthors = [[Chao Tang|Tang C]], [[Per Bak|Bak P]]
 | year = 1988
 | title = Mean field theory of self-organized critical phenomena
 | journal = [[Journal of Statistical Physics]]
 | volume = 51
 | issue = 5–6
 | pages = 797&ndash;802
 | doi = 10.1007/BF01014884
| bibcode= 1988JSP....51..797T
| s2cid = 67842194
 | url = https://zenodo.org/record/1232502
 | type = Submitted manuscript
 }}
</ref>), and examination of the conditions necessary for SOC to emerge. One of the important issues for the latter investigation was whether [[conservation of energy]] was required in the local dynamical exchanges of models: the answer in general is no, but with (minor) reservations, as some exchange dynamics (such as those of BTW) do require local conservation at least on average {{Clarify|date=July 2022}}.

It has been argued that the energy released in the BTW "sandpile" model should actually generate 1/f<sup>2</sup> noise rather than 1/f noise.<ref name=Jensen1989>
{{cite journal | vauthors = Jensen HJ, Christensen K, Fogedby HC | title = 1/f noise, distribution of lifetimes, and a pile of sand | journal = Physical Review B | volume = 40 | issue = 10 | pages = 7425–7427 | date = October 1989 | pmid = 9991162 | doi = 10.1103/physrevb.40.7425 | bibcode = 1989PhRvB..40.7425J }}
</ref> This claim was based on untested scaling assumptions, and a more rigorous analysis showed that sandpile models 
generally produce 1/f<sup>a</sup> spectra, with a<2.<ref name=Laurson2005>{{cite journal | vauthors = Laurson L, Alava MJ, Zapperi S |title=Letter: Power spectra of self-organized critical sand piles |journal=Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment |volume=0511 |id=L001 |date=15 September 2005 }}</ref>
However, the dynamics of the accumulated stress does exhibit the 1/f noise in the BTW model.<ref>{{Cite journal| vauthors = Shapoval A, Shnirman M | date=2024-07-01 | title = Explanation of flicker noise with the Bak-Tang-Wiesenfeld model of self-organized criticality|journal = Physical Review E | language = en | volume = 110 | issue=1 | article-number = 014106 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevE.110.014106 | pmid=39160903 | arxiv=2212.14726 | bibcode=2024PhRvE.110a4106S | issn = 2470-0053}}</ref>
Other simulation models were proposed later that could also produce true 1/f noise.<ref name=Maslov1999>{{cite journal | vauthors=[[S. Maslov|Maslov S]], [[C. Tang|Tang C]], [[Y. –C. Zhang|Zhang YC]] | year = 1999 | title = 1/f noise in Bak-Tang-Wiesenfeld models on narrow stripes | journal = [[Phys. Rev. Lett.]] | volume = 83 | issue = 12 | pages = 2449–2452 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.83.2449|arxiv = cond-mat/9902074 |bibcode = 1999PhRvL..83.2449M | s2cid = 119392131
 }}</ref>

In addition to the nonconservative theoretical model mentioned above {{Clarify|date=July 2022}}, other theoretical models for SOC have been based upon [[information theory]],<ref name=Dewar2003>{{cite journal | vauthors = Dewar R | year = 2003 | title = Information theory explanation of the fluctuation theorem, maximum entropy production and self-organized criticality in non-equilibrium stationary states | journal = Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General | volume = 36 | pages =631&ndash;641 | doi = 10.1088/0305-4470/36/3/303 | issue = 3 |bibcode = 2003JPhA...36..631D|arxiv = cond-mat/0005382 | s2cid = 44217479 | author-link = Roderick Dewar }}</ref> 
[[mean field theory]],<ref name=Vespignani1998>{{cite journal | vauthors = [[Alessandro Vespignani|Vespignani A]], [[Stefano Zapperi|Zapperi S]] | year = 1998 | title = How self-organized criticality works: a unified mean-field picture | journal = Physical Review E | volume = 57 | pages =6345–6362 | doi = 10.1103/physreve.57.6345 | issue = 6 | bibcode = 1998PhRvE..57.6345V | arxiv = cond-mat/9709192| hdl = 2047/d20002173 | s2cid = 29500701 }}</ref>
the [[convergence of random variables]],<ref name=Kendal2015>{{cite journal | vauthors = Kendal WS | year = 2015 | title = Self-organized criticality attributed to a central limit-like convergence effect | journal =Physica A | volume = 421 | pages =141&ndash;150 | doi = 10.1016/j.physa.2014.11.035|bibcode =2015PhyA..421..141K | author-link = Wayne Kendal }}</ref> and cluster formation.<ref name=Hoffmann2018b>{{cite journal | vauthors = Hoffmann H | title = Impact of network topology on self-organized criticality | journal = Physical Review E | volume = 97 | issue = 2–1 | article-number = 022313 | date = February 2018 | pmid = 29548239 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevE.97.022313 | author-link = Heiko Hoffmann | bibcode = 2018PhRvE..97b2313H | doi-access = free }}</ref> A continuous model of self-organised criticality is proposed by using [[tropical geometry]].<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Kalinin N, Guzmán-Sáenz A, Prieto Y, Shkolnikov M, Kalinina V, Lupercio E | title = Self-organized criticality and pattern emergence through the lens of tropical geometry | journal = Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America | volume = 115 | issue = 35 | pages = E8135–E8142 | date = August 2018 | pmid = 30111541 | pmc = 6126730 | doi = 10.1073/pnas.1805847115 | arxiv = 1806.09153 | doi-access = free | bibcode = 2018PNAS..115E8135K }}</ref>

Key theoretical issues yet to be resolved include the calculation of the possible [[universality class]]es of SOC behavior and the question of whether it is possible to derive a general rule for determining if an arbitrary [[algorithm]] displays SOC.

==In nature==
[[File:Sandpile Matemateca 19.jpg|thumb|The relevance of SOC to the dynamics of real sand has been questioned.]]
SOC has become established as a strong candidate for explaining a number of natural phenomena, including: 
* The magnitude of earthquakes ([[Gutenberg–Richter law]]) and frequency of aftershocks ([[Aftershock|Omori law]]) <ref name=TurcotteSmalleySolla85>{{cite journal | vauthors = Turcotte DL, Smalley Jr RF, Solla SA |author3-link=Sara Solla | year = 1985 | title = Collapse of loaded fractal trees | journal = Nature | doi= 10.1038/313671a0 | volume = 313 | issue = 6004 | pages = 671–672|bibcode = 1985Natur.313..671T 
|s2cid=4317400 }}</ref><ref name=SmalleyTurcotteSolla85 />
* Fluctuations in economic systems such as [[financial markets]] (references to SOC are common in [[econophysics]]) <ref>{{Cite journal | vauthors = Bak P, Paczuski M, Shubik M |date=1997-12-01 |title=Price variations in a stock market with many agents |journal=Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and Its Applications |language=en |volume=246 |issue=3 |pages=430–453 |doi=10.1016/S0378-4371(97)00401-9 |arxiv=cond-mat/9609144 |bibcode=1997PhyA..246..430B |s2cid=119480691 |issn=0378-4371}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | vauthors = Sornette D, Johansen A, Bouchaud JP |date= January 1996 |title=Stock Market Crashes, Precursors and Replicas |url=http://www.edpsciences.org/10.1051/jp1:1996135 |journal=Journal de Physique I |volume=6 |issue=1 |pages=167–175 |doi=10.1051/jp1:1996135 |arxiv= cond-mat/9510036 |bibcode= 1996JPhy1...6..167S |s2cid= 5492260 |issn=1155-4304}}</ref>
* The evolution of proteins<ref name=Phillips2014>{{cite journal | vauthors = Phillips JC | year = 2014 | title = Fractals and self-organized criticality in proteins | journal = Physica A | volume = 415 | pages = 440–448 | doi=10.1016/j.physa.2014.08.034 | bibcode = 2014PhyA..415..440P | author-link = James Charles Phillips
}}</ref><ref name=Phillips2021>{{cite journal | vauthors = Phillips JC | title = Synchronized attachment and the Darwinian evolution of coronaviruses CoV-1 and CoV-2 | journal = Physica A | volume = 581 | article-number = 126202 | date = November 2021 | pmid = 34177077 | pmc = 8216869 | doi = 10.1016/j.physa.2021.126202 | arxiv = 2008.12168 | author-link = James Charles Phillips | bibcode = 2021PhyA..58126202P }}</ref>
* Forest fires {{Clarify|date=July 2022}}<ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Malamud BD, Morein G, Turcotte DL | title = Forest fires: An example of self-organized critical behavior | journal = Science | volume = 281 | issue = 5384 | pages = 1840–1842 | date = September 1998 | pmid = 9743494 | doi = 10.1126/science.281.5384.1840 | bibcode = 1998Sci...281.1840M }}</ref>
* Neuronal avalanches in the cortex<ref name="Beggs2003" /><ref name=Poil2012>{{cite journal | vauthors = Poil SS, Hardstone R, Mansvelder HD, Linkenkaer-Hansen K | title = Critical-state dynamics of avalanches and oscillations jointly emerge from balanced excitation/inhibition in neuronal networks | journal = The Journal of Neuroscience | volume = 32 | issue = 29 | pages = 9817–9823 | date = July 2012 | pmid = 22815496 | pmc = 3553543 | doi = 10.1523/JNEUROSCI.5990-11.2012 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | vauthors = Chialvo DR |date=2010 |title=Emergent complex neural dynamics |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nphys1803 |journal=Nature Physics |language=en |volume=6 |issue=10 |pages=744–750 |doi=10.1038/nphys1803 |arxiv=1010.2530 |bibcode=2010NatPh...6..744C |s2cid=17584864 |issn=1745-2481}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | vauthors = Tagliazucchi E, Balenzuela P, Fraiman D, Chialvo DR | title = Criticality in large-scale brain FMRI dynamics unveiled by a novel point process analysis | journal = Frontiers in Physiology | volume = 3 | page = 15 | date = 2012 | pmid = 22347863 | pmc = 3274757 | doi = 10.3389/fphys.2012.00015 | doi-access = free }}</ref>
* [[Acoustic emission]] from fracturing materials<ref name=Caldarelli1996>{{cite journal | vauthors = Caldarelli G, Petri A | title = Self-Organization and Annealed Disorder in Fracturing Process | journal = Physical Review Letters | volume = 77 | issue = 12 | pages = 2503–2506 | date = September 1996 | pmid = 10061970 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.2503 | s2cid = 5462487 | bibcode = 1996PhRvL..77.2503C | url = https://backend.orbit.dtu.dk/ws/files/3992807/Guido.pdf }}</ref>

Despite the numerous applications of SOC to understanding natural phenomena, the universality of SOC theory has been questioned. For example, experiments with real piles of rice revealed their dynamics to be far more sensitive to parameters than originally predicted.<ref name=Frette1996>{{cite journal | vauthors = Frette V, Christensen K, Malthe-Sørenssen A, Feder J, Jøssang T, Meakin P | year = 1996 | title = Avalanche dynamics in a pile of rice | journal = [[Nature (journal)|Nature]] | volume = 379 | issue = 6560 | pages = 49–52 | doi =10.1038/379049a0 | bibcode= 1996Natur.379...49F| s2cid = 4344739 }}</ref><ref name=Bak1987/> Furthermore, it has been argued that 1/f scaling in EEG recordings are inconsistent with critical states,<ref name=Bedard2006>{{cite journal | vauthors = Bédard C, Kröger H, Destexhe A | title = Does the 1/f frequency scaling of brain signals reflect self-organized critical states? | journal = Physical Review Letters | volume = 97 | issue = 11 | article-number = 118102 | date = September 2006 | pmid = 17025932 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.97.118102 | arxiv = q-bio/0608026 | s2cid = 1036124 | bibcode = 2006PhRvL..97k8102B }}</ref> and whether SOC is a fundamental property of neural systems remains an open and controversial topic.<ref name=Hesse2014>{{cite journal | vauthors = Hesse J, Gross T | title = Self-organized criticality as a fundamental property of neural systems | journal = Frontiers in Systems Neuroscience | volume = 8 | page = 166 | year = 2014 | pmid = 25294989 | pmc = 4171833 | doi = 10.3389/fnsys.2014.00166 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

==Applications==
===Optimization===
It has been found that the avalanches from an SOC process make effective patterns in a random search for optimal solutions on graphs.<ref name=Hoffmann2018>
{{cite journal | vauthors = Hoffmann H, Payton DW | title = Optimization by Self-Organized Criticality | journal = Scientific Reports | volume = 8 | issue = 1 | page = 2358 | date = February 2018 | pmid = 29402956 | pmc = 5799203 | doi = 10.1038/s41598-018-20275-7  | doi-access = free| bibcode = 2018NatSR...8.2358H }}</ref> 
An example of such an optimization problem is [[graph coloring]]. The SOC process apparently helps the optimization from getting stuck in a [[local optimum]] without the use of any [[Simulated annealing|annealing]] scheme, as suggested by previous work on [[extremal optimization]].

===Synthetic biology===
Self-organized criticality has also been explored in [[synthetic biology]]. Experimental work has shown that [[gene regulatory networks]] engineered to operate near critical states can generate heterogeneous gene expression within genetically identical [[Cell (biology)|cell]] populations.<ref>{{cite journal | title = Engineering self-organized criticality in living cells | journal = Nature Communications | volume = 12 | page = 4415 | year = 2021 | doi = 10.1038/s41467-021-24695-4  | doi-access = free| first = Blai | last = Vidiella-Rocamora | pmc = 8292319 }}</ref> This behavior may reduce the need for precise tuning of [[protein]] production and has been proposed as a strategy to engineer functional diversity while maintaining a single genetic construct.<ref>{{cite journal | title = Synthetic criticality in cellular brains | journal = Journal of Physics: Complexity | year = 2021 | doi = 10.1088/2632-072X/ac35b3 | first = Ricard | last = Solé | hdl = 10230/52716 | hdl-access = free }}</ref>
